blocks: Confirmed first-year core and broader UCR study
Both explicitly develop first-year academic writing, presenting, source use, collaboration and reflection. UCR PPD is broader than this AI-specific practicum; the credits are not equivalent.
Both teach foundational programming through functions, data collections and classes. Their exact languages, exercises and code-review practices differ.
Both teach single-variable calculus, differentiation, integration and mathematical problem solving. UvA also includes multivariable calculus, which this relationship does not reproduce.
Both study fairness, privacy, responsibility, safety and societal effects of AI. UCR adds philosophical and psychological perspectives; detailed regulatory coverage differs.
Both implement and evaluate supervised and unsupervised machine-learning methods, model fit, validation and prediction.
Both develop vectors, matrices, subspaces, transformations, eigenmethods, least squares and singular value decomposition as computational foundations.
Both teach probability, inference, estimation and simulation, including Bayesian reasoning. UvA’s sustained conjugate-prior and Bayesian model-selection emphasis remains different.

Both teach mathematical optimisation for AI, including linear and discrete methods. UCR adds substantial agent search; this is not a claim to reproduce the whole convexity, simplex duality and integer-programming syllabus.

Both implement reinforcement-learning models. UvA investigates human learning and decisions; UCR develops learning agents, so the relationship covers a method rather than the complete cognitive syllabus.
The dedicated historical, scientific and social study of information-science turning points is not reproduced by an introductory programming or AI course.
The second AI-specific academic-skills practicum remains a distinct 1 EC component. Broader UCR research writing contributes to the programme, without a forced separate row relationship.
UCR optimisation and algorithms provide real search and problem-solving teaching, but do not reproduce this dedicated declarative Prolog and backtracking course. It remains deliberately unmatched.
